verses.saheeh: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe,
verses.khattab: Nũn. By the pen and what everyone writes
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Nūn, one of the letters of the alphabet: God knows best what He means by it. By the Pen, with which He has inscribed [the records of] all creatures in the Preserved Tablet, and what they inscribe, that is, the angels, of good and righteousness.
verses.romanUrdu: Noon, Kasam hai qalam ki aur us cheez ki jisey likhne waley likh rahey hain

verses.saheeh: You are not, [O Muhammad], by the favor of your Lord, a madman.
verses.khattab: By the grace of your Lord, you ˹O Prophet˺ are not insane
verses.jalalayn: ﻿You are not, O Muhammad (s), by the grace of your Lord, a madman, that is to say, madness is precluded in your case, on account of your Lord’s grace to you by way of [His assigning to you] prophethood and in other ways — this was a refutation of their saying that he was a madman.
verses.romanUrdu: Tum apne Rubb ke fazl se majnoon (deewane) nahin ho

verses.saheeh: And indeed, for you is a reward uninterrupted.
verses.khattab: You will certainly have a never-ending reward
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And assuredly you will have an unfailing reward.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur yaqeenan tumhare liye aisa ajar (reward) hai jiska silsila kabhi khatm honay wala nahin

verses.saheeh: And indeed, you are of a great moral character.
verses.khattab: And you are truly ˹a man˺ of outstanding character
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And assuredly you possess a magnificent nature, [a magnificent] religion.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur beshak tum akhlaaq ke bade martabe par ho

verses.saheeh: So you will see and they will see
verses.khattab: Soon you and the pagans will see
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then you will see and they will see,
verses.romanUrdu: Anqareeb tum bhi dekh logey aur woh bhi dekh lenge

verses.saheeh: Which of you is the afflicted [by a devil].
verses.khattab: which of you is mad
verses.jalalayn: ﻿which of you is demented (al-maftūn is a verbal noun, similar [in expressional form] to al-ma‘qūl, ‘intelligible’; al-futūn meaning al-junūn, ‘insanity’) in other words, is it [this insanity] in you or in them?
verses.romanUrdu: Ke tum mein se kaun junoon (madness) mein mubtala hai

verses.uthmani: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
verses.indopak: اِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ اَعْلَمُ بِمَنْ ضَلَّ عَنْ سَبِيْلِهٖ ۖ وَهُوَ اَعْلَمُ بِالْمُهْتَدِيْنَ
verses.transliteration: inna rabbaka huwa a'lamu biman dalla 'an sabeelihi wahuwa a'lamu bialmuhtadeena
verses.saheeh: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has gone astray from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
verses.khattab: Surely your Lord ˹alone˺ knows best who has strayed from His Way and who is ˹rightly˺ guided
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Assuredly your Lord knows best those who stray from His way, and He knows best those who are guided, to Him.
verses.romanUrdu: Tumhara Rubb un logon ko bhi khoob jaanta hai jo uski raah se bhatkey huey hain , aur wahi unko bhi acchi tarah jaanta hai jo raah-e-raast par hai

verses.saheeh: Then do not obey the deniers.
verses.khattab: So do not give in to the deniers
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So do not obey the deniers.
verses.romanUrdu: Lihaza tum in jhutlane walon ke dabao mein hargiz na aao

verses.saheeh: They wish that you would soften [in your position], so they would soften [toward you].
verses.khattab: They wish you would compromise so they would yield ˹to you˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They desire, they yearn, that (law relates to the verbal action) you should be pliable, [that] you should yield to them, so that they may be pliable [towards you], [so that] they may yield to you (fa-yudhinūna is a supplement to tudhinu, ‘you should be pliable’, but if it is understood to be the response to the optative clause of waddū, ‘they yearn’, then [a free standing pronoun] hum should be read as implied before it after the fā’ [sc. fa-hum yudhinūna]).
verses.romanUrdu: yeh to chahte hain ke kuch tum mudahnat (narmi) karo to yeh bhi mudahnat (narmi) karein

verses.saheeh: And do not obey every worthless habitual swearer
verses.khattab: And do not obey the despicable, vain oath-taker
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And do not obey any mean, despicable, oath-monger, given to frequent swearing by falsehood,
verses.romanUrdu: Hargiz na dabo kisi aisey shaks se jo bahut kasmein khane wala be-waqaat (worthless) aadmi hai

verses.saheeh: [And] scorner, going about with malicious gossip -
verses.khattab: slanderer, gossip-monger
verses.jalalayn: ﻿backbiting, faultfinder, that is to say, calumniator, scandal-monger, spreading [evil] talk among people in order to sow dissension between them,
verses.romanUrdu: Taaney deta hai , chugliyan khata phirta hai (slanderer, gossip-monger)

verses.saheeh: A preventer of good, transgressing and sinful,
verses.khattab: withholder of good, transgressor, evildoer
verses.jalalayn: ﻿hinderer of good, niggardly with his wealth against deserving causes, sinful transgressor, wrongdoer,
verses.romanUrdu: Bhalayi se rokta hai , zulm-o-zyadti mein hadd se guzar janey wala hai, sakht badh-amal hai , jafa-kaar hai

verses.saheeh: Cruel, moreover, and an illegitimate pretender.
verses.khattab: brute, and—on top of all that—an illegitimate child
verses.jalalayn: ﻿coarse-grained, crude, moreover ignoble, an adopted son of Quraysh — namely, al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra, whose father claimed him after eighteen years; Ibn ‘Abbās said, ‘We know of no one whom God has described in the derogatory way in which He describes him, blighting him with ignominy that will never leave him (the adverbial qualifier [ba‘da dhālika, ‘moreover’] is semantically connected to zanīm, ‘ignoble’) —
verses.romanUrdu: Aur in sab uyub (aib) ke saath badh-asl (illegitimate child) hai

verses.saheeh: Because he is a possessor of wealth and children,
verses.khattab: Now, ˹simply˺ because he has been blessed with ˹abundant˺ wealth and children
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[only] because (an should be understood as li-an, ‘because’, and it is semantically connected to that [meaning] which it is indicating) he has wealth and sons.
verses.romanUrdu: Is bina par ke woh bahut maal-o-aulad rakhta hai

verses.uthmani: إِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
verses.indopak: اِذَا تُتْلٰى عَلَيْهِ اٰيٰتُنَا قَالَ اَسَاطِيْرُ الْاَوَّلِيْنَ
verses.saheeh: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
verses.khattab: whenever Our revelations are recited to him, he says, “Ancient fables!”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿When Our signs — the Qur'an — are recited to him, he says, that they are [merely], ‘Fables of the ancients!’, in other words, he denies them [in arrogance] on account of the mentioned things which We have bestowed on him out of Our grace (a variant reading [for an of the previous verse] has [the interrogative] a-an).
verses.romanUrdu: Jab hamari aayat usko sunayi jati hai to kehta hai yeh to agle waqton ke afsane hain

verses.saheeh: We will brand him upon the snout.
verses.khattab: We will soon mark his snout
verses.jalalayn: ﻿We shall brand him on the snout: We shall leave a distinguishing mark upon his nose, one by which he will be reviled for as long as he lives; and so his nose was chopped off by a sword at Badr.
verses.romanUrdu: Ankareeb hum iski sund (snout) par daag lagayenge

verses.uthmani: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
verses.indopak: اِنَّا بَلَوْنٰهُمْ كَمَا بَلَوْنَاۤ اَصْحٰبَ الْجَـنَّةِ ۚ اِذْ اَقْسَمُوْا لَيَصْرِمُنَّهَا مُصْبِحِيْنَ ۙ
verses.transliteration: inna balawnahum kama balawna ashaba aljannati ith aqsamoo layasrimunnaha musbiheena
verses.saheeh: Indeed, We have tried them as We tried the companions of the garden, when they swore to cut its fruit in the [early] morning
verses.khattab: Indeed, We have tested those ˹Meccans˺ as We tested the owners of the garden—when they swore they would surely harvest ˹all˺ its fruit in the early morning
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Indeed We have tried them, We have tested the people of Mecca with drought and famine, just as We tried the owners of the garden, the orchard, when they vowed that they would pluck, [that] they would pick its fruits, in the morning, so that the poor folk would not notice them and so that they would not then have to give them of it that [portion] which their father used to give them of it by way of charity.
verses.romanUrdu: Humne in (ehle makkah) ko usi taraah aazmaish mein dala hai jis tarah ek baagh (garden) ke maalikon ko aazmaish mein dala tha, jab unhon ne kasam khayi ke subah sawerey zaroor apne baagh ke phal todenge

verses.saheeh: Without making exception.
verses.khattab: leaving no thought for Allah’s Will
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And they did not make any exception, to their vow, for God’s will (the sentence is a new [syntactically independent] one, in other words: and that was their condition).
verses.romanUrdu: Aur woh koi istasna (exception) nahin kar rahey thay

verses.uthmani: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفٞ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
verses.indopak: فَطَافَ عَلَيْهَا طَاۤٮِٕفٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّكَ وَهُمْ نَاۤٮِٕمُوْنَ
verses.saheeh: So there came upon the garden an affliction from your Lord while they were asleep.
verses.khattab: Then it was struck by a torment from your Lord while they slept
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Then a visitation from your Lord visited it, [that is] a fire consumed it during the night, while they slept.
verses.romanUrdu: Raat ko woh soye padey thay ke tumhare Rubb ki taraf se ek balaa is baagh par phir gayi

verses.saheeh: And it became as though reaped.
verses.khattab: so it was reduced to ashes
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So by the morning it was like the darkness of night, in other words, black.
verses.romanUrdu: Aur uska haal aisa ho gaya jaise kati hui fasal ho

verses.saheeh: And they called one another at morning,
verses.khattab: Then by daybreak they called out to each other
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They then called out to one another in the morning,
verses.romanUrdu: Subah un logon ne ek dusre ko pukara

verses.uthmani: أَنِ ٱغۡدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡثِكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰرِمِينَ
verses.indopak: اَنِ اغْدُوْا عَلٰى حَرْثِكُمْ اِنْ كُنْتُمْ صٰرِمِيْنَ
verses.saheeh: [Saying], "Go early to your crop if you would cut the fruit."
verses.khattab: ˹saying,˺ “Go early to your harvest, if you want to pick ˹all˺ the fruit.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿[saying], ‘Go forth early to your tillage, your produce (ani’ghdū ‘alā harthikum constitutes an explication of [the import of] tanādaw, ‘they called out to one another’; otherwise, an relates to the verbal action, [to be understood as] being bi-an) if you are going to pluck’, if your intention is to pick [the fruits] (the response to the conditional is indicated by what preceded it).
verses.romanUrdu: Kaha agar phal todne hai ho to sawerey sawerey apni kheti ki taraf nikal chalo

verses.saheeh: So they set out, while lowering their voices,
verses.khattab: So they went off, whispering to one another
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So off they went, whispering to one another, talking secretly:
verses.romanUrdu: Chunanchey woh chal padey aur aapas mein chupke chupke kehte jatay thay

verses.uthmani: أَن لَّا يَدۡخُلَنَّهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّسۡكِينٞ
verses.indopak: اَنْ لَّا يَدْخُلَنَّهَا الْيَوْمَ عَلَيْكُمْ مِّسْكِيْنٌ ۙ
verses.saheeh: [Saying], "There will surely not enter it today upon you [any] poor person."
verses.khattab: “Do not let any poor person enter your garden today.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿‘No needy person shall today come to you in it’ (this constitutes the explication of the preceding [verse]; or else, an relates to the verbal action, [to be understood] to mean bi-an).
verses.romanUrdu: Ke aaj koi miskeen tumhare paas baag mein na aane paye

verses.saheeh: And they went early in determination, [assuming themselves] able.
verses.khattab: And they proceeded early, totally fixated on their purpose
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And they went forth early, supposing themselves, able to prohibit, to prevent the poor folk [from enjoying the fruit].
verses.romanUrdu: Woh kuch na dene ka faisla kiye huye subah sawerey jaldi jaldi is tarah wahan gaye jaise ke woh (phal todne par) qadir hain

verses.saheeh: But when they saw it, they said, "Indeed, we are lost;
verses.khattab: But when they saw it ˹devastated˺, they cried, “We must have lost ˹our˺ way
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But when they saw it, blackened and charred, they said, ‘Assuredly we have strayed!’, from it, that is to say: this is not the one. Then when they recognised it, they said:
verses.romanUrdu: Magar jab baagh ko dekha to kehne lagey “hum raasta bhool gaye hain

verses.saheeh: Rather, we have been deprived."
verses.khattab: In fact, we have been deprived ˹of our livelihood˺.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿‘Nay, but we have been deprived!’, of its fruits, by our denying it to the poor folk.
verses.romanUrdu: Nahin balke hum mehroom reh gaye”

verses.uthmani: قَالَ أَوۡسَطُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ لَوۡلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
verses.indopak: قَالَ اَوْسَطُهُمْ اَلَمْ اَقُلْ لَّكُمْ لَوْلَا تُسَبِّحُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: qala awsatuhum alam aqul lakum lawla tusabbihoona
verses.saheeh: The most moderate of them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Why do you not exalt [Allah]?' "
verses.khattab: The most sensible of them said, “Did I not urge you to say, ‘Allah willing.’?”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿The most moderate, the best one, among them said, ‘Did I not say to you, “Why do you not glorify?” ’, God, repenting [to Him].
verses.romanUrdu: Un mein jo sab se behtar aadmi tha usne kaha “maine tumse kaha na tha ke tum tasbeeh kyun nahin karte?”

verses.uthmani: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
verses.indopak: قَالُوْا سُبْحٰنَ رَبِّنَاۤ اِنَّا كُنَّا ظٰلِمِيْنَ
verses.saheeh: They said, "Exalted is our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
verses.khattab: They replied, “Glory be to our Lord! We have truly been wrongdoers.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They said, ‘Glory be to God, our Lord. Verily we have been wrongdoers’, by denying the poor folk [what is] their due.
verses.romanUrdu: Woh pukar utthey paak hai hamara Rubb, waqayi hum gunahgaar thay

verses.saheeh: Then they approached one another, blaming each other.
verses.khattab: Then they turned on each other, throwing blame
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They then turned to one another, blaming each other.
verses.romanUrdu: Phir unmein se har ek dusre ko malamat karne laga

verses.saheeh: They said, "O woe to us; indeed we were transgressors.
verses.khattab: They said, “Woe to us! We have certainly been transgressors
verses.jalalayn: ﻿They said, ‘O ([yā is] for calling attention to something) woe to us!, [O] destruction of ours. We have indeed been unjust.
verses.romanUrdu: Akhir ko unhon ne kaha “afsos hamare haal par, beshak hum sarkash ho gaye thay

verses.uthmani: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَنَا خَيۡرٗا مِّنۡهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
verses.indopak: عَسٰى رَبُّنَاۤ اَنْ يُّبْدِلَـنَا خَيْرًا مِّنْهَاۤ اِنَّاۤ اِلٰى رَبِّنَا رٰغِبُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: 'asa rabbuna an yubdilana khayran minha inna ila rabbina raghiboona
verses.saheeh: Perhaps our Lord will substitute for us [one] better than it. Indeed, we are toward our Lord desirous."
verses.khattab: We trust our Lord will give us a better garden than this, ˹for˺ we are indeed turning to our Lord with hope.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿It may be that our Lord will give us in its place (read yubaddilanā or yubdilanā) one that is better than it. Truly we turn humbly to our Lord’, that He might accept our repentance and give us back [a garden that is] better than our garden — it is reported that they were indeed given a better one in its place.
verses.romanUrdu: Baeed (door) nahin ke hamara Rubb humein badle mein issey behtar baagh ata farmaye, hum apne Rubb ki taraf rujoo karte hain

verses.uthmani: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡعَذَابُ ۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُ ۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
verses.indopak: كَذٰلِكَ الْعَذَابُ ۗ وَلَعَذَابُ الْاٰخِرَةِ اَكْبَرُ ۘ لَوْ كَانُوْا يَعْلَمُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: kathalika al'athabu wala'athabu alakhirati akbaru law kanoo ya'lamoona
verses.saheeh: Such is the punishment [of this world]. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
verses.khattab: That is the ˹way of Our˺ punishment ˹in this world˺. But the punishment of the Hereafter is certainly far worse, if only they knew
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Such, that is to say, like the chastisement for these [people], will be the chastisement, for those disbelievers of Mecca and others who contravene Our command; and the chastisement of the Hereafter is assuredly greater, did they but know, its chastisement, they would not have contavened Our command. When they said ‘If we are resurrected, we shall be given better than [what] you [have been given], the following was revealed:
verses.romanUrdu: Aisa hota hai azaab aur aakhirat ka azaab issey bhi bada hai, kaash yeh log isko jaante

verses.uthmani: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
verses.indopak: اِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِيْنَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ جَنّٰتِ النَّعِيْمِ
verses.saheeh: Indeed, for the righteous with their Lord are the Gardens of Pleasure.
verses.khattab: Indeed, the righteous will have the Gardens of Bliss with their Lord
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Verily for the God-fearing there will be the Gardens of Bliss near their Lord.
verses.romanUrdu: Yaqeenan khuda-tars logon ke liye unke Rubb ke yahan niyamat bhari jannatein hain

verses.saheeh: Then will We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
verses.khattab: Should We then treat those who have submitted like the wicked
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Are We then to treat those who submit [to Us] as [We treat] the sinners?, that is to say, as belonging with them in terms of reward?
verses.romanUrdu: Kya hum farma-bardaaron ka haal mujreemon sa kardein

verses.saheeh: What is [the matter] with you? How do you judge?
verses.khattab: What is the matter with you? How do you judge
verses.jalalayn: ﻿What is wrong with you? How do you judge?, with such corrupt judgement?
verses.romanUrdu: Tum logon ko kya ho gaya hai, tum kaise hukum lagate ho

verses.saheeh: Or do you have a scripture in which you learn
verses.khattab: Or do you have a scripture, in which you read
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Or (am lakum means a-lakum) do you have a Scripture, revealed, wherein you learn, [wherein] you read,
verses.romanUrdu: Kya tumhare paas koi kitaab hai jismein tum yeh padhte ho

verses.saheeh: That indeed for you is whatever you choose?
verses.khattab: that you will have whatever you choose
verses.jalalayn: ﻿that you will indeed have in it whatever you choose?
verses.romanUrdu: Ke tumhare liye zaroor wahan wahi kuch hai jo tum apne liye pasand karte ho

verses.uthmani: أَمۡ لَكُمۡ أَيۡمَٰنٌ عَلَيۡنَا بَٰلِغَةٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ إِنَّ لَكُمۡ لَمَا تَحۡكُمُونَ
verses.indopak: اَمْ لَـكُمْ اَيْمَانٌ عَلَيْنَا بَالِغَةٌ اِلٰى يَوْمِ الْقِيٰمَةِ ۙ اِنَّ لَـكُمْ لَمَا تَحْكُمُوْنَ ۚ
verses.transliteration: am lakum aymanun 'alayna balighatun ila yawmi alqiyamati inna lakum lama tahkumoona
verses.saheeh: Or do you have oaths [binding] upon Us, extending until the Day of Resurrection, that indeed for you is whatever you judge?
verses.khattab: Or do you have oaths binding on Us until the Day of Judgment that you will have whatever you decide
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Or do you have oaths, pledges, binding, secured, on Us until the Day of Resurrection (ilā yawmi’l-qiyāmati is semantically connected to ‘alaynā, ‘on Us’; these words [‘alaynā bālighatun, ‘binding on Us’] contain the sense of an oath [given], in other words, ‘Did We swear to you?’, the response to which is [what follows]) that you will indeed have whatever you decide?, to have for yourselves.
verses.romanUrdu: Ya phir kya tumhare liye roz-e-qayamat tak humpar kuch ahad-o-paiman (covenant) sabit hai ke tumhein wahi kuch milega jiska tum hukum lagao

verses.saheeh: Ask them which of them, for that [claim], is responsible.
verses.khattab: Ask them ˹O Prophet˺ which of them can guarantee all that
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Ask them, which of them will aver, will guarantee for them, that?, [that] decision which they have made for themselves, namely, that they will be given better [reward] than the believers in the Hereafter?
verses.romanUrdu: Inse pucho tum mein se kaun iska zaamin (gurantee/responsible) hai

verses.uthmani: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ شُرَكَآءُ فَلۡيَأۡتُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمۡ إِن كَانُواْ صَٰدِقِينَ
verses.indopak: اَمْ لَهُمْ شُرَكَاۤءُ ۚ فَلْيَأْتُوْا بِشُرَكَاۤٮِٕهِمْ اِنْ كَانُوْا صٰدِقِيْنَ
verses.transliteration: am lahum shurakao falyatoo bishurakaihim in kanoo sadiqeena
verses.saheeh: Or do they have partners? Then let them bring their partners, if they should be truthful.
verses.khattab: Or do they have associate-gods ˹supporting this claim˺? Then let them bring forth their associate-gods, if what they say is true
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Or do they have partners?, who agree with them in this claim of theirs and able to guarantee it for them; if that is the case: Then let them produce their partners, those who will guarantee this for them, if they are truthful.
verses.romanUrdu: Ya phir inke thehraye huye kuch sahreek hain (jinhon ne iska zimma liya ho)?yeh baat hai to layein apne shareekon ko agar yeh sacchey hain

verses.uthmani: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقٖ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
verses.indopak: يَوْمَ يُكْشَفُ عَنْ سَاقٍ وَّيُدْعَوْنَ اِلَى السُّجُوْدِ فَلَا يَسْتَطِيْعُوْنَ ۙ
verses.transliteration: yawma yukshafu 'an saqin wayud'awna ila alssujoodi fala yastatee'oona
verses.saheeh: The Day the shin will be uncovered and they are invited to prostration but the disbelievers will not be able,
verses.khattab: ˹Beware of˺ the Day the Shin ˹of Allah˺ will be bared, and the wicked will be asked to prostrate, but they will not be able to do so
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Mention, the day when the shank is bared (an expression denoting the severity of the predicament during the reckoning and the requital on the Day of Resurrection: one says kashafati’l-harbu ‘an sāqin, ‘the war has bared its shank’, to mean that it has intensified) and they are summoned to prostrate themselves, as a test of their faith, but they will not be able [to do so] — their backs will become as [stiff as] a brick wall.
verses.romanUrdu: Jis roz sakht waqt aa padega aur logon ko sajda karne ke liye bulaya jayega to yeh log sajda na kar sakenge

verses.uthmani: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةٞ ۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
verses.indopak: خَاشِعَةً اَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ ۗ وَقَدْ كَانُوْا يُدْعَوْنَ اِلَى السُّجُوْدِ وَهُمْ سٰلِمُوْنَ
verses.transliteration: khashi'atan absaruhum tarhaquhum thillatun waqad kanoo yud'awna ila alssujoodi wahum salimoona
verses.saheeh: Their eyes humbled, humiliation will cover them. And they used to be invited to prostration while they were sound.
verses.khattab: with eyes downcast, totally covered with disgrace. For they were ˹always˺ called to prostrate ˹in the world˺ when they were fully capable ˹but they chose not to˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿With humbled (khāshi‘atan is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person [of the verb] yud‘awna, ‘they are summoned’) that is to say, with abject, gazes, which they do not raise, they will be overcast, enveloped, by abasement; for they had indeed been summoned, in this world, to prostrate themselves while they were yet sound, but they never used to do it, by the fact that they never performed prayer.
verses.romanUrdu: Inki nigaahein nichey hongi, zillat inpar chaa rahi hogi. Yeh jab sahi-o-saalim thay us waqt inhein sajde ke liye (bulaya jata tha) aur yeh inkar karte thay

verses.uthmani: فَذَرۡنِي وَمَن يُكَذِّبُ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡحَدِيثِ ۖ سَنَسۡتَدۡرِجُهُم مِّنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
verses.indopak: فَذَرْنِىْ وَمَنْ يُّكَذِّبُ بِهٰذَا الْحَـدِيْثِ ۗ سَنَسْتَدْرِجُهُمْ مِّنْ حَيْثُ لَا يَعْلَمُوْنَ ۙ
verses.transliteration: fatharnee waman yukaththibu bihatha alhadeethi sanastadrijuhum min haythu la ya'lamoona
verses.saheeh: So leave Me, [O Muhammad], with [the matter of] whoever denies the Qur'an. We will progressively lead them [to punishment] from where they do not know.
verses.khattab: So leave to Me ˹O Prophet˺ those who reject this message. We will gradually draw them to destruction in ways they cannot comprehend
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So leave Me [to deal] with those who deny this discourse — the Qur'an. We will draw them on by degrees, We will seize them little by little, whence they do not know.
verses.romanUrdu: Pas aey Nabi, tum is kalam ke jhutlane walon ka maamla mujhpar chodh do hum aise tarike se inko batadreej tabahi ki taraf le jayenge ke inko khabar bhi na hogi

verses.saheeh: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
verses.khattab: I ˹only˺ delay their end for a while, but My planning is flawless
verses.jalalayn: ﻿And I will grant them respite; [for] assuredly My devising is firm, [My devising is] severe and cannot be withstood.
verses.romanUrdu: Main inki rassi daraaz kar raha hoon, meri chaal badi zabardast hai

verses.uthmani: أَمۡ تَسۡـَٔلُهُمۡ أَجۡرٗا فَهُم مِّن مَّغۡرَمٖ مُّثۡقَلُونَ
verses.indopak: اَمْ تَسْـَٔـلُهُمْ اَجْرًا فَهُمْ مِّنْ مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُوْنَ ۚ
verses.transliteration: am tasaluhum ajran fahum min maghramin muthqaloona
verses.saheeh: Or do you ask of them a payment, so they are by debt burdened down?
verses.khattab: Or are you asking them for a reward ˹for the message˺ so that they are overburdened by debt
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Or are you asking them a fee, in return for delivering the Message, so that they are weighed down with debt?, [so that they are weighed down] with what they will [have to] give you, and that is why they do not believe.
verses.romanUrdu: Kya tum insey koi ajar (compensation) talab kar rahey ho ke yeh is chatti ke bojh (feel burdened with debt) taley dabey ja rahe hoon

verses.saheeh: Or have they [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down?
verses.khattab: Or do they have access to ˹the Record in˺ the unseen, so they copy it ˹for all to see˺
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Or do they possess [access to] the Unseen, that is, [access to] the Preserved Tablet which contains [knowledge of] the Unseen, so that they are writing down?, from it what they say.
verses.romanUrdu: Kya inke paas gaib ka ilam hai jisey yeh likh rahey hon

verses.uthmani: فَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلۡحُوتِ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكۡظُومٞ
verses.indopak: فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُنْ كَصَاحِبِ الْحُوْتِ ۘ اِذْ نَادٰى وَهُوَ مَكْظُوْمٌ ۗ
verses.transliteration: faisbir lihukmi rabbika wala takun kasahibi alhooti ith nada wahuwa makthoomun
verses.saheeh: Then be patient for the decision of your Lord, [O Muhammad], and be not like the companion of the fish when he called out while he was distressed.
verses.khattab: So be patient with your Lord’s decree, and do not be like ˹Jonah,˺ the Man of the Whale, who cried out ˹to Allah˺, in total distress
verses.jalalayn: ﻿So await patiently the judgement of your Lord, regarding them in the way that He wills, and do not be like the one of the whale, in terms of impatience and haste — this is Jonah, peace be upon him — who called out, [who] supplicated his Lord, choking with grief, filled with anguish inside the belly of the whale.
verses.romanUrdu: Pas apne Rubb ka faisla saadir honay tak sabr karo aur machli wale (younis) ki tarah na ho jao, jab usne pukara tha aur woh gham se bhara hua tha

verses.uthmani: لَّوۡلَآ أَن تَدَٰرَكَهُۥ نِعۡمَةٞ مِّن رَّبِّهِۦ لَنُبِذَ بِٱلۡعَرَآءِ وَهُوَ مَذۡمُومٞ
verses.indopak: لَوْلَاۤ اَنْ تَدٰرَكَهٗ نِعْمَةٌ مِّنْ رَّبِّهٖ لَنُبِذَ بِالْعَرَاۤءِ وَهُوَ مَذْمُوْمٌ
verses.transliteration: lawla an tadarakahu ni'matun min rabbihi lanubitha bial'arai wahuwa mathmoomun
verses.saheeh: If not that a favor from his Lord overtook him, he would have been thrown onto the naked shore while he was censured.
verses.khattab: Had he not been shown grace by his Lord, he would have certainly been cast onto the open ˹shore˺, still blameworthy
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Had it not been for a grace, a mercy, from his Lord that reached him, he would have surely been cast, out of the belly of the whale, onto a wilderness, a desolate land, while he was blameworthy — but he was shown mercy and was therefore cast out blameless.

wbw.translation: surely he would have been thrown

verses.romanUrdu: Agar uske Rubb ki meharbani uske shamil-e-haal na ho jati to woh mazmoom (disgrace) hokar chatyal maidan mein phenk diya jata

verses.saheeh: And his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
verses.khattab: Then his Lord chose him, making him one of the righteous
verses.jalalayn: ﻿But his Lord chose him, for prophethood, and made him one of the righteous, the prophets.
verses.romanUrdu: Aakhir-e-kaar uske Rubb ne usey barguzida (exalted) farma liya aur usey saleh bandon mein shamil kardiya

verses.uthmani: وَإِن يَكَادُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَيُزۡلِقُونَكَ بِأَبۡصَٰرِهِمۡ لَمَّا سَمِعُواْ ٱلذِّكۡرَ وَيَقُولُونَ إِنَّهُۥ لَمَجۡنُونٞ
verses.indopak: وَاِنْ يَّكَادُ الَّذِيْنَ كَفَرُوْا لَيُزْلِقُوْنَكَ بِاَبْصَارِهِمْ لَمَّا سَمِعُوا الذِّكْرَ وَيَقُوْلُوْنَ اِنَّهٗ لَمَجْنُوْنٌ ۘ
verses.transliteration: wain yakadu allatheena kafaroo layuzliqoonaka biabsarihim lamma sami'oo alththikra wayaqooloona innahu lamajnoonun
verses.saheeh: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their eyes when they hear the message, and they say, "Indeed, he is mad."
verses.khattab: The disbelievers would almost cut you down with their eyes when they hear ˹you recite˺ the Reminder, and say, “He is certainly a madman.”
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Indeed those who disbelieve would almost throw you down [to the ground] (read la-yuzliqūnaka or la-yazliqūnaka) with their looks, looking at you in a severe way, almost hurling you to the ground or making you fall from your place, when they hear the Reminder, the Qur'an, and they say, out of envy: ‘He is truly a madman!’, on account of the Qur'an that he has brought.
verses.romanUrdu: Jab yeh kafir log kalam-e-nasihat (Quran) sunte hain to tumhein aisi nazaron se dekhte hain ke goya tumhare qadam ukhaad denge, Aur kehte hain ke yeh zaroor deewana hai

verses.saheeh: But it is not except a reminder to the worlds.
verses.khattab: But it is simply a reminder to the whole world
verses.jalalayn: ﻿Yet it, namely, the Qur'an, is just a Reminder, an admonition, for all the worlds, of [both] humans and jinn, and cannot be the cause of any dementia.
verses.romanUrdu: Halaanke yeh to sarey jahaan walon ke liye ek naseehat hai
